decisions.statement: Every job this system runs goes up the same way.
A commit origin does not carry is pushed there before the job goes up.
A commit origin still does not carry after the push refuses the run.
A commit that reaches origin nowhere puts no job up.
The secrets the job reads are placed before the job goes up.
A key no secret page places refuses the run rather than leaving the job to fail.
A job is put up by reading its manifest off standard input.
The run waits for the job to end rather than answering while it runs.
A job that failed is seen on the round it failed rather than after the wait.
How many rounds a job is waited is the caller's to say.
A job that ended either way has every line it said read and carried back.
A job that failed refuses the run, and the lines still come back.
A job left running past the wait refuses the run rather than being taken away.
Every job runs in the namespace named here.
Nothing here reads what a job's lines mean.

definition: a job put on the cluster at a commit, waited on, and answered as what it said
